question: How many official languages does India have as per the 8th Schedule of the Constitution as on 30th June 2022?
solution:
The correct answer is __**22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The Eighth Schedule to the constitution of India lists the official languages of India. There is a total of 22 languages as the official languages. While 14 languages are included earlier and the rest of the languages were added to the constitution through subsequent amendments.

 
• Part XVII of the Indian constitution deals with the official languages in Articles 343 to 351.
 
• Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Oriya, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri are the languages that are included in the Constitution. 
 
• 14 were initially included in the Constitution. 
 
• The Sindhi language was added by the 21st Amendment Act of 1967.
 
• Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali were included by the 71st Amendment Act of 1992.
 
• Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali were added by the 92nd Amendment Act of 2003 which came into force in 2004.
 
• There are six languages Classical languages: Tamil (declared in 2004), Sanskrit (2005), Kannada (2008), Telugu (2008), Malayalam (2013), and Odia (2014). 
 
• The Constitutional provisions related to the Eighth Schedule are Article 344 and Article 351.

 Thus, it is concluded that there are 22 languages mentioned in the 8th Schedule of the Indian constitution.
